biography.plain_text: Robbie W. Smith is an American counsellor and co-founder of Safe Harbor Boys Home in Jacksonville, Florida. Trained in counselling psychology, she and her husband Doug established the nonprofit in 1984 after caring for teenagers facing juvenile detention. She has served as executive director, using education, mentoring and practical maritime training to support adolescent boys.

long_biography.plain_text:
Before Safe Harbor became her life's work, Robbie W. Smith worked as a child therapist. In 1982, she and her husband Doug agreed to care temporarily for boys facing detention, changing plans for an early retirement. The experience persuaded them to create a structured residential programme, formally incorporating the nonprofit in Jacksonville in 1984.

Smith trained in counselling psychology and later led Safe Harbor as executive director, clinical director and chief executive. Its model combines schooling, mentoring, vocational instruction and seamanship to help teenagers develop responsibility and practical skills. She and Doug committed their own resources during the organisation's early years and continued without salaries, while outside donors supported the programme. Their work later inspired the television film Safe Harbor.
